records.source: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος· εἴ τις ἐπισκοπῆς ὀρέγεται, καλοῦ ἔργου ἐπιθυμεῖ.
records.gloss: Trustworthy [is] the saying: if anyone overseership aspires to, a good work he desires.
pieces: Here is a saying you can rely on: anyone who wants to be an overseer is setting their heart on a good work.

L.1: The saying [is] trustworthy: if anyone aspires to [the office of] overseer, he desires a good work.

R.1: Here is something true: if someone wants to be a leader who watches over the church, they want to do a good work.

decisions.choice: "the saying is trustworthy" goes with what follows
alternatives: it goes with 2:15, the verse before
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates the formula as introducing verse 1. Elsewhere it usually points to a well-known statement of faith (1:15; 4:9), and some readers take it with 2:15 instead. A few manuscripts read "the saying is human", "commonly said".

decisions.choice: overseership: the work of an overseer of the church
alternatives: the office of a bishop in the later sense
decisions.reason: ἐπισκοπῆς is oversight; the overseer (verse 2) is a leader who watches over the church, the same people called elders in Titus 1:5-7 and Acts 20:17, 20:28 (compare Philippians 1:1). The later pattern of one bishop over many churches is not in view.

decisions.choice: if anyone: any member who aspires to it
decisions.reason: τις is general, though the qualifications that follow (verse 2) are written with men in view.

decisions.choice: an overseer (B); a leader who watches over the church (R)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:1, "bishop" would suggest a later office (m2).

records.heading: What an overseer must be

records.source: δεῖ οὖν τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνεπίλημπτον εἶναι, μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρα, νηφάλιον, σώφρονα, κόσμιον, φιλόξενον, διδακτικόν, μὴ πάροινον, μὴ πλήκτην, ἀλλὰ ἐπιεικῆ, ἄμαχον, ἀφιλάργυρον, τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου καλῶς προϊστάμενον, τέκνα ἔχοντα ἐν ὑποταγῇ μετὰ πάσης σεμνότητος·
records.gloss: It is necessary therefore the overseer above reproach to be, of one wife husband, sober, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, \v 3 not a drunkard, not violent, but gentle, peaceable, not a lover of money, \v 4 his own household well managing, children having in submission with all dignity
pieces: So an overseer must be someone no one can fairly criticize: faithful to his one wife, clear-headed, self-controlled, respected, welcoming to guests, able to teach,
not a heavy drinker, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not someone who loves money.
He must manage his own household well and see that his children obey him and are respectful in every way.

L.2: Therefore the overseer must be above reproach, the husband of one wife, sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach,
L.3: not given to drunkenness, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money,
L.4: managing his own household well, keeping [his] children in submission with all dignity.

R.2: So a church leader must live in a way that no one can say anything bad about him. He must have only one wife. He must keep his mind clear, control himself, and live a good life. He must be happy to welcome guests into his home, and he must be able to teach.
R.3: He must not drink too much wine or fight with people. He must be gentle and peaceful, and he must not love money.
R.4: He must lead his own family well, and his children must obey him and respect him.

decisions.choice: above reproach: giving no one grounds to accuse
decisions.reason: ἀνεπίλημπτον heads the list: the qualities that follow spell it out.

decisions.choice: the husband of one wife: faithful to one wife
decisions.reason: The Greek is literally "a one-woman man". It may mean faithful in marriage, married only once (compare 5:9 of widows), or not having more than one wife; the order of words stresses "one". It is not clearly a requirement that he be married (Paul himself was not, 1 Corinthians 7:7-8).

decisions.choice: sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach
decisions.reason: νηφάλιον is clear-headed; σώφρονα sensible, self-controlled; κόσμιον orderly, respectable; φιλόξενον welcoming to strangers, important when believers traveled; διδακτικόν able to teach, the one quality that concerns the work itself.

decisions.choice: not given to wine, not violent
decisions.reason: πάροινον is one who sits long over wine; πλήκτην one who strikes others.

decisions.choice: children in submission with all dignity: the dignity may be the father's or the children's
decisions.reason: μετὰ πάσης σεμνότητος may describe how the father keeps order (with dignity) or the children's respectful behavior.

decisions.choice: faithful to his one wife
decisions.reason: Balanced states the sense chosen in m2, which is uncertain; Literal keeps the Greek wording.

decisions.choice: He must have only one wife
decisions.reason: Readable keeps close to the Greek wording, leaving the question of m2 open.

records.source: εἰ δέ τις τοῦ ἰδίου οἴκου προστῆναι οὐκ οἶδεν, πῶς ἐκκλησίας θεοῦ ἐπιμελήσεται μὴ νεόφυτον, ἵνα μὴ τυφωθεὶς εἰς κρίμα ἐμπέσῃ τοῦ διαβόλου.
records.gloss: if but anyone his own household to manage not knows, how [the] church of God will he care for? \v 6 not a new convert, so that not being puffed up into [the] judgment he may fall of the devil.
pieces: (If someone does not know how to manage his own household, how can he take care of God's church?)
He must not be a recent convert, or he may become proud and fall under the same judgment as the devil.

L.5: (But if anyone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for [the] church of God?)
L.6: [He must] not [be] a new convert, so that he may not become conceited and fall into the condemnation of the devil.

R.5: If a man cannot lead his own family, how can he take care of God's church?
R.6: A church leader must not be someone who has only just become a believer. If he is, he might become proud. Then he would be judged, as the devil was judged.

decisions.choice: a question inside the list
decisions.reason: Verse 5 breaks into the list to give a reason; the list resumes in verse 6.

decisions.choice: a new convert: one newly planted
decisions.reason: νεόφυτον means newly planted, a recent believer.

decisions.choice: the condemnation of the devil: the judgment the devil fell under
decisions.reason: τοῦ διαβόλου may mean the judgment passed on the devil for his pride, or the accusation the devil brings. The parallel in verse 7 ("the snare of the devil") supports the second; "puffed up" supports the first.
Literal and Balanced mark verse 5 as an aside (m1).

records.source: δεῖ δὲ καὶ μαρτυρίαν καλὴν ἔχειν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔξωθεν, ἵνα μὴ εἰς ὀνειδισμὸν ἐμπέσῃ καὶ παγίδα τοῦ διαβόλου.
records.gloss: It is necessary but also testimony good to have from those outside, so that not into disgrace he may fall and [the] snare of the devil.
pieces: He must also be well thought of by outsiders, so that he does not fall into disgrace and into the devil's trap.

L.7: And he must also have a good testimony from outsiders, so that he may not fall into disgrace and the snare of the devil.

R.7: People who are not believers must also think well of him. Then no one will be able to say bad things about him, and the devil will not be able to trap him.

decisions.choice: a good testimony from outsiders: a good reputation among unbelievers
decisions.reason: "Those outside" are people outside the church (1 Thessalonians 4:12; Colossians 4:5).

decisions.choice: the snare of the devil: a trap the devil sets
decisions.reason: Disgrace before outsiders can trap a leader into further wrong (2 Timothy 2:26).

records.source: Διακόνους ὡσαύτως σεμνούς, μὴ διλόγους, μὴ οἴνῳ πολλῷ προσέχοντας, μὴ αἰσχροκερδεῖς, ἔχοντας τὸ μυστήριον τῆς πίστεως ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει.
records.gloss: Deacons likewise dignified, not double-tongued, not to wine much given, not greedy for dishonest gain, \v 9 holding the mystery of the faith with a clean conscience.
pieces: In the same way, deacons must be worthy of respect, sincere in what they say, not heavy drinkers, and not greedy for money.
They must hold on to the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.

L.8: Deacons likewise [must be] dignified, not double-tongued, not given to much wine, not greedy for dishonest gain,
L.9: holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.

R.8: In the same way, deacons who serve in the church must be people others respect. They must not say one thing and mean another. They must not drink too much wine or try to get money in dishonest ways.
R.9: They must hold on to the mystery of the faith that God has made known, and live with a clear conscience.

decisions.choice: deacons: those who serve the church
decisions.reason: Διακόνους is a servant; here, as in Philippians 1:1, a recognized group in the church alongside the overseers. The letter does not describe their duties.

decisions.choice: double-tongued: saying one thing to one person and another to another
decisions.reason: διλόγους is found only here: two-worded, insincere.

decisions.choice: the mystery of the faith: the gospel, God's hidden plan now made known
decisions.reason: μυστήριον is God's plan once hidden and now revealed (Colossians 1:26-27); "of the faith" is what believers believe. Verse 16 sets out its content.

decisions.choice: deacons who serve in the church
decisions.reason: Readable says what deacons are (m1).

decisions.choice: the mystery of the faith that God has made known
decisions.reason: Readable explains "mystery" and keeps the key term (m3).

records.heading: Deacons

records.source: καὶ οὗτοι δὲ δοκιμαζέσθωσαν πρῶτον, εἶτα διακονείτωσαν ἀνέγκλητοι ὄντες.
records.gloss: And these also let be tested first, then let them serve being blameless.
pieces: They too should first be tested; then, if no charge can be brought against them, let them serve.

L.10: And let these also be tested first; then let them serve, if they are blameless.

R.10: First the church should test them to see what kind of people they are. If no one can blame them for anything, they can serve as deacons.

decisions.choice: let them be tested first: their character examined over time
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζω is to test and approve. The verse does not describe a formal procedure.

records.source: γυναῖκας ὡσαύτως σεμνάς, μὴ διαβόλους, νηφαλίους, πιστὰς ἐν πᾶσιν.
records.gloss: Women likewise dignified, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.
pieces: The women likewise must be worthy of respect, not slanderers, clear-headed and trustworthy in everything.

L.11: Women likewise [must be] dignified, not slanderers, sober-minded, faithful in all things.

R.11: In the same way, the women must be people others respect. They must not say bad things about others. They must keep their minds clear and be faithful in everything.

decisions.choice: women: women deacons, or the wives of deacons
decisions.reason: γυναῖκας can mean "women" or "wives". Placed in the middle of the section on deacons, with "likewise" as in verse 8, it may name women who served as deacons (Phoebe is called "deacon of the church" in Romans 16:1), or deacons' wives; there is no "their" to settle it.

decisions.choice: slanderers: the word used for the devil
decisions.reason: διαβόλους is the word translated "devil" in verses 6-7, here in its ordinary sense of slanderer.

records.source: διάκονοι ἔστωσαν μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἄνδρες, τέκνων καλῶς προϊστάμενοι καὶ τῶν ἰδίων οἴκων·
records.gloss: Deacons let be of one wife husbands, children managing well and their own households;
pieces: A deacon must be faithful to his one wife and manage his children and household well.

L.12: Let deacons be husbands of one wife, managing [their] children and their own households well.

R.12: Each deacon must have only one wife. He must lead his children and his family well.

decisions.choice: husbands of one wife
decisions.reason: The same phrase as verse 2 (see the note there).

decisions.choice: faithful to his one wife
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: οἱ γὰρ καλῶς διακονήσαντες βαθμὸν ἑαυτοῖς καλὸν περιποιοῦνται καὶ πολλὴν παρρησίαν ἐν πίστει τῇ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: those for well having served a standing for themselves good gain and much confidence in faith the [one] in Christ Jesus.
pieces: Those who serve well earn a good standing for themselves and great boldness in their faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

L.13: For those who have served well gain a good standing for themselves and great confidence in the faith that is in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.

R.13: Those who serve well will be respected. They will also be very sure of their faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus.

decisions.choice: a good standing: a step, a good position
alternatives: a higher rank in the church
decisions.reason: βαθμὸν is a step or grade, and so standing. It most likely means respect in the church and before God, not promotion.

decisions.choice: confidence: boldness
decisions.reason: παρρησίαν is freedom and boldness, in speaking and before God.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

records.source: Ταῦτά σοι γράφω, ἐλπίζων ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ἐν τάχει, ἐὰν δὲ βραδύνω, ἵνα εἰδῇς πῶς δεῖ ἐν οἴκῳ θεοῦ ἀναστρέφεσθαι, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐκκλησία θεοῦ ζῶντος, στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς ἀληθείας·
records.gloss: These things to you I write, hoping to come to you soon; \v 15 if but I delay, so that you may know how it is necessary in [the] household of God to conduct oneself, which is [the] church of God living, a pillar and foundation of the truth.
pieces: I am writing you these things, though I hope to come to you soon,
so that, if I am delayed, you will know how people ought to live in God's household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth.

L.14: I am writing these things to you, hoping to come to you soon;
L.15: but if I am delayed, [I write] so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the household of God, which is [the] church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth.

R.14: I hope to come to you soon. But I am writing these things to you now,
R.15: in case I am delayed. Then you will know how people should live as members of God's family. That family is the church of the living God. It holds up the truth and keeps it safe, like a pillar and a foundation hold up a building.

decisions.choice: the household of God: God's family, the church
decisions.reason: οἴκῳ is a house or household. The rules for overseers and deacons are rules for God's household (compare 3:4-5).

decisions.choice: how one ought to conduct oneself: anyone in the household
alternatives: how you, Timothy, ought to conduct yourself
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; it may mean Timothy or anyone in the church.

decisions.choice: a pillar and foundation of the truth: the church holds up and supports the truth
decisions.reason: στῦλος is a pillar, ἑδραίωμα a foundation or support. The picture may come from the great temple of Artemis at Ephesus, famous for its columns. The church upholds the truth by holding to it and making it known.

decisions.choice: It holds up the truth and keeps it safe, like a pillar and a foundation hold up a building
alternatives: a pillar and foundation of the truth
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m3).

records.heading: The mystery of our faith

records.source: καὶ ὁμολογουμένως μέγα ἐστὶν τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας μυστήριον· Ὃς ἐφανερώθη ἐν σαρκί, ἐδικαιώθη ἐν πνεύματι, ὤφθη ἀγγέλοις, ἐκηρύχθη ἐν ἔθνεσιν, ἐπιστεύθη ἐν κόσμῳ, ἀνελήμφθη ἐν δόξῃ.
records.gloss: And confessedly great is the of godliness mystery: who was revealed in flesh, was vindicated in spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among nations, was believed on in [the] world, was taken up in glory.
pieces: Beyond all question, the mystery of our faith is great: He was revealed in a human body, vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed in throughout the world, taken up in glory.

L.16: And by common confession great is the mystery of godliness: [He] who was revealed in [the] flesh, was vindicated in [the] Spirit, was seen by angels, was proclaimed among [the] nations, was believed on in [the] world, was taken up in glory.

R.16: Everyone agrees that the mystery of our faith, which God has made known, is great: {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} appeared as a human being. The Spirit showed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was right with God. Angels saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. People told about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to all the nations. People in the world believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. God took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up into heaven in glory.

decisions.choice: by common confession great is the mystery of godliness
decisions.reason: ὁμολογουμένως means "as all agree, confessedly". εὐσεβείας μυστήριον is the hidden truth now revealed that lies at the heart of true godliness: the person of Christ, as the lines that follow describe.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "who"
decisions.reason: The earliest manuscripts read Ὃς ("who"). Many later manuscripts read "God", which in early Greek writing differs from "who" by two small strokes, and some read "which", agreeing with "mystery". "Who" is the harder reading, since it has no stated antecedent, and best explains the others; it refers to Christ.

decisions.choice: a hymn or confession in six lines
decisions.reason: The six short lines, each a verb with a phrase, have the shape of an early Christian hymn or confession (compare Philippians 2:6-11). They pair opposites: flesh and spirit, angels and nations, world and glory.

decisions.choice: vindicated by the Spirit: shown to be in the right, in his resurrection
decisions.reason: δικαιόω means to justify or declare in the right. Set against "flesh", "in Spirit" may mean by the Holy Spirit, who raised him (Romans 1:4; 8:11), or in the realm of the Spirit. Either way his resurrection showed him to be in the right.

decisions.choice: taken up in glory: his ascension
decisions.reason: ἀναλαμβάνω is the verb used of Jesus' ascension (Acts 1:2, 1:11, 1:22).

decisions.choice: the mystery of our faith
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose godliness: the faith of believers (m1). The key term "mystery" is kept.

decisions.choice: He (B); Christ (R)
decisions.reason: "Who" has no antecedent in the sentence; it is Christ (m2).

decisions.choice: God took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up into heaven in glory
decisions.reason: Readable names God and says where he was taken (m5).
